The SMART system is a line side material delivery system that reduces 4 wall and line side inventory in support of FPS Synch. Material Flow and empower Production Operators to determine when material is needed at line side. Three Process, SMART Card is used globally and store  inventory usage by scanning kan-ban cards each cycle; SMART Call, used globally, mechanises the request process, allowing a lineside button press to trigger material replenishment which in turn stores inventory usage; SMART AutoCall, used globally, based on approx. inventory levels at lineside and BoM requirements for each vehicle, triggers SMART Call-style material replenish., again storing usage for analysis. For all three types of SMART, a part can be classified as an eSMART part for these parts, each delivery instance is sent electronically to suppliers via the eSMART. The application does not include primary supplier call-in, and does not deal with financials or purchasing of inventory, or the reporting of inventory levels

SERL is a web-based application that facilitates the input, review, approval, and implementation of window label standard equipment. Access to edit standard equipment is available in MOCM to ensure that only the VLMMs have update capability. The Data Dictionary section within SERL houses standard equipment descriptions by Sales Division. The Data Dictionary assists with providing accurate and consistent descriptions across vehicle lines within each Sales Division. SERL uses the MOCM security table to identify valid VLMM CDS IDs and authorize changes and additions. The VLMM accesses the Data Dictionary directly from the SERL home page (www.serl.ford.com).

Description: The Service Loss Assignment system's main goal is to determine the reason for service loss (i.e., local fill & system fill loss) for PDC stocked parts in N.A.  The SLA output data will be used as the basis for applying operational or system changes to help improve fill. SLA fill calculations were designed to match the currently used PA0012PR Fill report from MMP Network12 & will provide drill-down capability into the data. The reason for all service loss will be gauged by probing the entire supply chain (from supplier shipment to final PDC stockkeep transaction) to show where a process may have been over standard. SLA will use data processed by the IMAS application to decide the cause for service loss.  IT Architecture: SLA information is staged on DB2 to facilitate DB2 table lookups & then stored on Teradata & accessed via both interactive web screens & a data analysis-reporting tool called Business Objects.  Business Criticality: Med-H Additional Outage Impact includes: Impact to Financial Results.

An Intranet application designed to initiate the transactions that will transfer dealer and customer accounts from a closing branch to one or more receiving branches. Three types of transactions can be created. 1.) Full Branch Transfer - Where the entire portfolio of a closing branch is transferred to a single receiving branch. 2.) Partial Branch Transfer - Where the portfolio of a closing branch is being transferred to 2 or more receiving branches. 3.) Liquidating Branch Transfer - Where the accounts of branches closed prior to PTA are merged with the dealers previously created in the new branch. On-line and batch reports will also be created to provide the branches with a cross reference of the old dealer number (ex. ABA100) and the new dealer number (ex. AKA100).    Dealer Web services functionalities are provided to FCNA down streams to extract dealer data.

OneSumX FS IFRS9 is a financial application provided by Wolters Kluwer that uses contract data to calculate Expected Credit Loss amounts over contract lifetime. IFRS9/CECL is an accounting standard that addresses the treatment of Expected Credit Losses (ECL). These ECL amounts are then aggregated by the particular market and posted to the General Ledger. This information will be publicly available as part of the balance sheet for Ford Credit, thus making it a SOX application. 10 markets are currently in scope - FCE, US, Canada, Mexico and China. The contract scope is for the retail markets. The ECL for wholesale contracts is out of scope and will be calculated manually. OneSumX will start to generate EAD/ECL calculations from take on date (TOD). The contractual outstanding principal that FORD CREDIT is required to deliver should be the principal outstanding amount at TOD. FORD CREDIT is also required to deliver the contractual accrued interest from the contractual last repayment date to TOD.

The Active Directory Federation Service ADFS provides a Ford Motor Company centralized Multiple Domain Single-Sign-On solution for web based applications.  ADFS uses the Security Assertion Markup Language SAML and the WS-Federation framework to securely and directly communicate information about application users between Ford Motor Company and trusted partners.  ADFS acts as either an identity provider or a service provider depending on the needs of the partner application.    The Identity Provider role is used to gather required user attributes - generate a Federated Response-Assertion Document, sign the document, encrypt the document, and redirect the browser with the Federated Response-Assertion Document to the federated partners server acting in the Service Provider Role.  The Service Provider is used to decrypt the Federated Response-Assertion Document provided by the federated partners server acting in the Identity Provider Role, verify the signature of the Document, and pass the validated user

DNS (Domain Name System) is a standard Internet protocol that provides name-to-address resolution of servers and applications, allowing a user to connect to an easily remembered name like myapp.ford.com, rather than an esoteric IP address like 19.9.9.9. DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) is a standard Internet protocol that automatically configures workstation network information such as IP address, default router, DNS server, etc., eliminating the need to manually administer this information on each machine. IP Address Management (IPAM) software tracks IP Address allocation and manages distributed enterprise DNS and DHCP services. Use of an IPAM generates consistent and syntactically correct configuration files, reducing DNS and DHCP errors, and allowing delegation of day-to-day data administration to Level-1 site administrators.

This method of communication is non-graphical and consists of purely standard ASCII characters. HOD sessions are pre-configured java applets that are deployed to any standard web server. The java applet connects to a specified host based on the pre-configuration data and produces a Green Screen session within the client's browser.

GSDB CRP is a global application used to support the process of Buyers requesting changes (updates or additions) to GSDB Supplier Data. It was initially funded by EU Accounts Payable with an aim to ensure that high-quality data, especially European tax information, is input into GSDB. Process (up to 2008), Buyers were asked to complete a complex, multi-tiered form. This was often filled in incorrectly or is incomplete, which in turn can lead to significant errors, for instance in the amount of tax that Ford pays. This web-based application ensures, where possible, that the end user will only be required to input data that is relevant to their request. This will be done by intelligently reducing the number of fields shown dependent on the type of request e.g. location of requestor, Prod vs. NonProd, type of GSDB site being requested etc. The tool will seamlessly feed the requests into GSDB and will be used primarily by the Buyers (to request change) and the DMA's (to approve and implement those changes).

GOLFF is a forecasting application used for material forecast for the next 18 months. The main purpose of GOLFF application is to send a 6 months forecast file to CMMS3. CMMS3 in turn uses it for supplier release. GOLFF reads the entity data from SPCPS and deducts the year to date actual and the segmented in-plant orders, this produces a balance-to-go volume for each Market entity. GOLFF then overlays orders from the Sales bank with Estimated Build dates/periods into the appropriate dates and then uses the remaining undated orders to fill in more gaps. The resultant balance-to-go is then forecast by GOLFF using the most recent historical data (3 months Demand Intelligence or DI) thus completing the requirements through the whole future 6 month period. The 80 column order images created in GOLFF are then exploded via GPAM Solve table to generate SFI volumes which in turn are converted into actual manufacturing parts. The parts volume data is then transmitted through CMMS3 to all Suppliers on a weekly basis.

The FTM (File Transfer Management) system allows file transfers from server to server through different platforms using a WEB interface. The technology requires System Analyst, Supervisor and ITI analysts. The process begins with the System Development staff supplying all information required in the FTM web page. The next step involves the supervisors responsible for transferring approvals and the last step involves Support Analysts that are responsible to validate all parameters and identify the gaps based on infrastructure information. The FTM has a database to retrieve the parameters (sFTP information). The servers and scripts do the transfers automatically based on the parameters informed by System Analysts and validated by ITI Analysts. The scripts and servers require ITI support to analyze if the servers runs the sFTP script and the analysts will also be responsible to check the servers and update the sFTP script. This technology supports Brazil, Venezuela, Argentina and Mexico ADS teams.

The Microsoft Windows Active Directory glossary defines an Active Directory as a structure supported by Windows that lets any object on a network be tracked and located. Active Directory is the directory service used in Windows Server and provides the foundation for Windows distributed networks. A directory service provides the methods for storing directory data and making this data available to network users and administrators. For example, Active Directory stores information about user accounts, such as names, phone numbers, and so on, and enables other authorized users on the same network to access this information.    The AD, or Active Directory, is a database based on the LDAP (Lightweight Directory Access Protocol) standard, which makes the information contained within the AD easily available to other applications across different platforms. DNS (Domain Name System) is a standard Internet protocol that provides name-to-address resolution of servers and applications, allowing a user to connect to an easily remembered name like myapp.ford.com, rather than an esoteric IP address like 19.9.9.9. DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) is a standard Internet protocol that automatically configures workstation network information such as IP address, default router, DNS server, etc., eliminating the need to manually administer this information on each machine. IP Address Management (IPAM) software tracks IP Address allocation and manages distributed enterprise DNS and DHCP services. Use of an IPAM generates consistent and syntactically correct configuration files, reducing DNS and DHCP errors, and allowing delegation of day-to-day data administration to Level-1 site administrators.

OneSumX FS IFRS9 is a financial application provided by Wolters Kluwer that uses contract data to calculate Expected Credit Loss amounts over contract lifetime. IFRS9/CECL is an accounting standard that addresses the treatment of Expected Credit Losses (ECL). These ECL amounts are then aggregated by the particular market and posted to the General Ledger. This information will be publicly available as part of the balance sheet for Ford Credit, thus making it a SOX application. 10 markets are currently in scope - FCE, US, Canada, Mexico and China. The contract scope is for the retail markets. The ECL for wholesale contracts is out of scope and will be calculated manually. OneSumX will start to generate EAD/ECL calculations from take on date (TOD). The contractual outstanding principal that FORD CREDIT is required to deliver should be the principal outstanding amount at TOD. FORD CREDIT is also required to deliver the contractual accrued interest from the contractual last repayment date to TOD.

Description: Host On Demand (HOD) is a thin client terminal emulation solution. Thin client being a java applet rather than the traditional, fat client, operating system specific executable file,ie (Windows EXE file). HOD is a solution for communicating with servers using a terminal interface commonly called Green Screen Emulation. This method of communication is non-graphical and consists of purely standard ASCII characters. HOD sessions are pre-configured java applets that are deployed to any standard web server. The java applet is accessed through a web page link that, in turn, will run inside the client's web browser. The java applet connects to a specified host based on the pre-configuration data and produces a Green Screen session within the client's browser.

The Active Directory Federation Service ADFS provides a Ford Motor Company centralized Multiple Domain Single-Sign-On solution for web based applications.  ADFS uses the Security Assertion Markup Language SAML and the WS-Federation framework to securely and directly communicate information about application users between Ford Motor Company and trusted partners.  ADFS acts as either an identity provider or a service provider depending on the needs of the partner application.    The Identity Provider role is used to gather required user attributes - generate a Federated Response-Assertion Document, sign the document, encrypt the document, and redirect the browser with the Federated Response-Assertion Document to the federated partners server acting in the Service Provider Role.  The Service Provider is used to decrypt the Federated Response-Assertion Document provided by the federated partners server acting in the Identity Provider Role, verify the signature of the Document, and pass the validated user
